# CASEs with `line` `pragmatic-transport`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Contextual pragmatic information transport** — what survives when an utterance is translated, retold or rendered in another medium — communicative identity as relationally organized observables, and fidelity as directed, task-relative transport between observational systems.

| [CASE-324](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-324.md) | Coupled meaning–influence model vs cut models | [LEAD-029](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-029.md) asked for a joint prediction of the pragmatic-transport and will-organization lines, derived through [CLAIM-336](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md)'s mapping with flexibility penalized, and for the comparison of one model against separate models that A55 §7 states and [ARG-065](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-065.md) holds. Data were simulated from an instance of [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s equations: three operators, four contexts (frames), a scalar meaning state read out as a noisy response, and governance interventions that boost or suppress one operator's authority. The joint model (16 parameters) was fitted beside a model with the loop cut (15), the same with more freedom (19), and an interpretation model plus a governance model (18), on the same 240 training episodes, and all were scored on the effects of interventions in compositions not seen in training. With the loop present the joint model's error was 0.0013 to 0.0185, against 0.0062 to 0.0504 for the best separate model; with the loop present but misspecified, about half; with no loop it tied the cut model and the BIC preferred the cut model. The world is built and the joint model is its family, so the study shows that the test has power and what the prediction is, not that any real system has the loop. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

Between-subjects respondents give two free binary answers in one of four contexts; true models are Lo et al.'s Table 1 and a symmetric family with Δ_C from −0.3 to 0.3 and signalling from 0 to 0.6. The plug-in test is valid, but at Δ_C = 0.19 and no true signalling its power is 0.24 at 2,500 respondents a context and 0.65 at 4,000; with signalling of 0.3, 0.80 at 1,600. Absence by the plug-in bound is invalid (84% on the boundary); a Bonferroni bound is valid and can show absence only where signalling is small. Nothing here is a finding about judgements. In the null (one configuration, three random O(d) frames, 1000 draws at each of three sizes), the largest ‖H − I‖ is 2.2e-14. In the planar case, the holonomy angle equals the sum of the internal angles in 12 of 12 draws. Local log-map charts of the sphere give a holonomy within 0.3% of the triangle's spherical excess. With representation noise σ, the null's holonomy has median about 1.3σ at ten anchors per overlap, but with three anchors up to 23% of draws flip orientation. | [CASE-344](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-344.md) | PMI additivity in text8 along WordNet | Co-occurrence was counted in text8, about 17M tokens of English Wikipedia: 10 000 target words against 5 000 context words, in a window of ±5. The PMI was shrunk so that it stays finite at zero counts. Analogy families: in each word2vec quadruple, the PMI interaction P_a − P_b − P_c + P_d holds a noise-corrected median share of 0.21 to 0.30 of the quadruple's variation, against 0.33 for random quadruples. No family is near additive. But families with less interaction complete more often in a rank-300 embedding (Spearman −0.83 over 14 families), and within 13 of 14 families the least-interacting third of quadruples completes more often than the most-interacting third (0.59 against 0.31). Hierarchy: 4 315 nouns with 590 WordNet ancestor attributes. A held-out-word additive fit explains about 3.5% of the double-centred PMI variance, about 6% of its reliable part (split-half reliability 0.58), against about −0.6% for the same attributes on permuted words. Deeper attributes add to it. Linear probes on low-rank embeddings reach balanced accuracy of about 0.70–0.80, with no fall by WordNet depth. Their false positives fall inside the attribute's parent about twice as often as chance. No language-model annotation was used. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-359](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-359.md) | Signalling estimators, binary contextuality | Run in session for [LEAD-072](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-072.md) on 2026-11-22 (scratch/studies/lead-072; sig.py with 9 passing tests, exact.py, mc.py, floor.py, apply.py; seeds fixed). Exact enumeration per content and 4,000-replication simulations of correlated rank-2 systems at 2 to 100 occurrences a context. The plug-in Δ's bias at zero signalling is 1.5 at two occurrences and 0.22 at a hundred; the root of the unbiased squared difference cuts it by half or more and falls short at large Δ. The simultaneous Clopper-Pearson interval never covered below 0.999; Newcombe's approximate one fell to 0.93. The Bonferroni-Fisher test kept its size (at most 0.034 at 5%) and cannot reject at all below three occurrences. On [LIT-842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-842.md)'s printed systems, at the least counts their fractions allow, one signals by the interval, one by the test alone, one by neither; a fourth table is inconsistent as printed. [LIT-851](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-851.md) could not be used. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CASE-371](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-371.md) | Toy transformer forgetting study | A toy-scale stand-in for [CASE-274](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-274.md)'s design, for [LEAD-043](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-043.md). numpy only, CPU, about two hours of compute on a shared machine. A two-layer transformer (d 64, 4 heads, no layer norm, hand-written backward pass) memorizes 256 random facts under two query templates. 32 target facts are then fine-tuned away in seven arms: unlearning toward a uniform output, gradient ascent and overwriting with new values, each at one cue or two, with rehearsal of the rest; and an unrelated new task without rehearsal. Every model has a twin trained from the same initialization on a world that differs only in the target values, so every readout has a false-positive rate. Pooled over 4 seeds and both worlds, in the unlearning, overwriting and new-task arms 87 to 98 percent of the forgotten facts are recovered by at least one reader, against 28 to 46 percent for the twin's values, and the average fact is recovered by 2.8 to 3.6 readers against 0.4 to 1.0. An untrained cue recovers 73 to 79 percent when one cue was fine-tuned; reverting one early block's update restores 41 to 55 percent; relearning half the targets makes the second fine-tuned-away value faster to learn after overwriting or a new task (8 to 8.5 steps against 17.5 to 25.5 for the twin). Gradient ascent instead collapses the model (retained facts at 8 to 19 percent), and run past its criterion leaves no reader above baseline. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CASE-385](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-385.md) | Permutation-aligned MLPs and loss barriers | [LEAD-157](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-157.md)'s design run at toy scale on CPU. Two-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs are trained in numpy on a task with two redundant cues, A and B. A test that uses no barrier says which cue each net relies on: its accuracy when only A, or only B, carries the label. Pairs are aligned four ways (none, weight matching, activation matching, and rescaling quotiented before weight matching), and at width 5 by an exhaustive search over permutations plus optimised rescaling. The barrier is then measured on the straight line, a trained Bezier curve and a trained one-bend polychain. The aligned linear barrier falls with width for every kind of pair. At width 5, three of four pairs that both rely on cue A keep a loss barrier of 0.09 to 0.25 after the exhaustive search, about as much as pairs relying on different cues (0.15 to 0.54). At widths 64 and 256 an A-net and a B-net are connected after activation matching (0.000). A copy of a net, permuted and rescaled per unit, computes exactly the same function, yet permutation alignment alone leaves it a barrier of 0.19 to 0.59. In a load-by-temperature grid, one cell is flat and poorly connected without alignment. There, alignment plus a trained curve removes the barrier, while the aligned straight line keeps 0.07 error, and the cell's accuracy deficit stays. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-398](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-398.md) | Logit subspaces in GPT-2 small and Pythia-70m | [LEAD-073](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-073.md) asked for [NOTE-746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-746.md)'s M, N and Γ_q in released models, for relations where linearity has been reported. Forward passes of GPT-2 small and Pythia-70m, in numpy on CPU, gave the final-layer-norm output f(x) over about 3,200 contexts, and the unembeddings gave G. Exactly, both models meet the diversity condition: the unembeddings span the whole space, and the final layer norm's bias leaves every f(x) with a fixed nonzero component off the hyperplane its normalisation confines it to, so F is the whole space too. Then M = N = ℝᵈ and the containments Γ ⊆ N and Γ_q ⊆ M hold for any relation. At the tolerance stated before the run (singular values above 1e-3 of the largest; at most 1% of any direction outside), they fail for all three relations tested (city in country, country language, country capital) in GPT-2 small, whose context spectrum is dominated by one direction, and fail narrowly for Γ ⊆ N in Pythia-70m, where f is constant, to within 2.4e-4, along one direction. A post-hoc sweep shows the verdict turning on the tolerance. City in country is fairly linear in GPT-2 small (held-out R² 0.82); the other relations less so. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-417](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-417.md) | BERT anaphora study reanalysed | Run for [LEAD-191](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-191.md). [LIT-844](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-844.md)'s 51,966,480 PR-like models of the binary 3-cycle were to be reanalysed by the sheaf test it applies (CF > 2\|M\|·SF) and by CbD 2.0. The per-instance BERT probabilities are not published, so the full reanalysis was not possible. Linear programs confirm that the sheaf verdict is SF < 1/6 and the CbD 2.0 verdict Δ < 2, and that the first set lies inside the second. The published counts then fix the divergence: 36,861,830 instances (70.9%), all CbD-contextual and not sheaf-contextual. The 25 printed instances split 9 / 8 / 7 / 1. Code, tests and results are in scratch/studies/lead-191/. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
